The pet project Homer is forced to abandon so he can work on his magic bat.
When given a choice between Crab Juice and a certain sugary soft drink, Homer chooses the crab juice--several cans of it. Unfortunately there's no nearby bathroom....
Grown in the jungle primeval by inmates of a South American insane asylum, these mercilessly hot peppers are the fuel for Homer's mystical journey to find his soul mate.
Homer's dream recliner, purchased for him by his long-lost Brother Herb.
The ancient and revered artifact that is most sacred to the secret order of Stonecutters. Used as a bib and hanky by Homer. Also used to clean his ears.
Homer's greatest rival at work. The inanimate carbon rod first beat him out for employee of the month, then was credited with saving the space shuttle crew upon re-entry.
The mascot for a popular Japanese cleaning product, that just happens to bear an uncanny resemblance to Homer J. Simpson.
Trying to impress some older kids, Bart cuts the head off the statue commemorating the town's founder.
What initially seemed like another lame present from Homer is put to good use by Bart when he uses it to fool the entire town into thinking that a kid is trapped at the bottom of a well.
Bart wanted this game so bad, he almost ended up doing hard time.
Also known as "Buttzilla," this ordinary weather balloon was vandalized by Bart to resemble Principal Skinner.
Bart's beloved childhood doll, with head removed, used as Lisa's good luck charm during the big hockey game.
Fake, of course. Obviously Bart is too young to drive.
One of the countless products receiving the official Krusty Brand Seal of Approval. May cause birth defects.
This fossilized "angel skeleton" was actually part of a publicity stunt for Heavenly Hills Mall.
Lisa's answer to the sexist, vacuous talking Malibu Stacy doll. Alternative names for the doll suggested by Bart: "Blabbermouth - The Jerky Doll for Jerks," "Wendy Windbag," and "Ugly Doris."
Originally intended for someone else, Lisa gave this valentine to Ralph out of shear pity, a kindness she came to regret.
Lisa becomes obsessive as a result of a teacher's strike and finds ways to learn on her own.
Because the Simpsons do not have a dental plan, Lisa must settle for a cheaper set of braces that "pre-date stainless steel" so she can't get them wet.
Lisa's futuristic favorite snack in her college years as told by a fortune-teller.
Homer may no longer have his Mr. Plow business, but Marge won't let him get rid of the jacket.
Marge proves her artistic skill by revealing the inner beauty of a naked, ugly Monty Burns.
The only love letter Marge ever received from Homer, written on the back of a Postcard from the Duff Brewery in Capital City in 1978.
Homer gave a beautiful green bowling ball, engraved "Homer," to Marge for her birthday.
The red blazer representing the principles and ideals of the real estate industry.
Homer "gets" 2nd prize at a contest put on by the local radio station: a free boudoir photography session.
From Marge's brief stint as a police officer. Homer enjoys a squirt of pepper spray on his eggs in the morning.
Newly vegetarian Lisa gets a laugh when Apu shows her a t-shirt with the words, "Don't have a cow, man" on it.
The shirt worn by Homer's bowling team: Homer, Moe, Apu, and, unfortunately, Mr. Burns.
Protest sign wielded by an ignorant mob member protesting illegal immigrants, including Apu.
Apu is reduced to lying on the floor like a farm animal to feed his eight children.
Worn by Homer in a vain, last minute attempt to halt the arranged marriage ceremony of Apu and Manjula.
Apu invents a new type of Squishee which is tasted once, and only once, by Bart and then thrown in a dumpster.
The filth encrusted hot dog that got Apu briefly fired from the Kwik-E-Mart.
Purchased by Bart, Milhouse and Martin for a 100 dollars. The ensuing fight over ownership resulted in the valuable comic book being reduced to a tattered, destroyed mess.
The most popular personalized license plate available at the Itchy and Scratchy Land gift shop. "Bart" is nowhere to be found.
A memento from one of Bart's many brushes with greatness, when he was the beloved "I didn't do it" boy.
Bart makes a collect call to Australia which sparks an international conflict requiring him to make a formal public apology in Australia. The Australians want to punish him with "the Boot."
Part of Scratchy's arm on an animation cell. Bart paid 300 dollars for it and then extorted the cash from Mr. Burns.
A multitalented dummy outperformed Krusty and took over his timeslot and his fans.
Lisa's stolen hamster from her "Is my brother dumber than a hamster?" experiment.
When Homer runs out of donuts at work, he sells his soul to Devil Flanders for a tasty donut.
This talking doll was bent on murdering Homer, until the repairman was called in to set its switch to "good" instead of "evil."
The cookbook used by Kodos to prepare fried shrimp for Lisa, sloppy Joe's for Bart, pork chops for Homer, and radish rosettes for Marge.
Homer accidently turned his toaster into a time machine, thus doing irreparable harm to the space-time continuum.
After Snake's execution, his body was carved up for organs and Homer got Snakes hair transplanted onto his head.
A cursed "Monkey's Paw" sold to Homer by the former President of Algeria.
Willie died on the thirteenth hour, of the thirteenth day, of the thirteenth month at a PTA meeting in Springfield Elementary--according to the school's calendar.
